items.title: fix(sequence): emit the whole ordered adjustment when a note reaches several messages
items.body:
## Problem and value

Closes #903.

On the reported draft (owner at `y: 300` with a note wrapping onto the blockers at `y: 330` and `y: 366`), the `sequence/note-overlap` receipt advertised `set /messages/1/y to 399` — a move that jumps the first blocker past the second one, reordering the timeline — and the follow-up run then reported the same failure for blocker `/messages/2/y` with `supportedFixes: []`. The diagnostic's repair model was single-blocker while the failure reaches several messages, so the documented repair loop stalled exactly where the issue measured it (26 of 26 targeted multi-blocker configurations, 3 of 354 random documents).

The receipt now carries **one ordered adjustment for every message the note reaches**: the first reached message takes the first clear slot at or below `requiredY`, each following one the first clear slot below the previous, every candidate verified through the same readability predicate a single move uses. Both repair paths now share one invariant — a repair never moves a message past one the note does not reach, because that would silently reorder the timeline — and an arrangement that cannot hold (no authored room, a crossing, a content-limit breach) advertises `[]` instead of a broken edit.

PR improvement check (`CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-improvement-check`): test-value (implementation mode) drove the suite toward user-visible outcomes — the advertised set applies to a clean document, a withhold keeps the document honest — instead of source-shape assertions; simplifying the single- and multi-blocker paths onto the shared `moveCeiling` predicate removed the duplicated crowding cap that caused the forced `+28` spacing, and the moved-message clone now drops its memoized note layout so a long scan does not accumulate dead entries.

## What changed

- `archify/renderers/sequence/render-sequence.mjs` — the note-overlap repair is now an ordered joint adjustment:
  - `noteReachedMessages` lists every message the wrapped note reaches, y-ordered; the multi-blocker receipt carries them all in `evidence.reached` and the human message counts the rest (`and N more message(s) below`).
  - `noteOverlapAdjustment` places each reached message on the first clear slot at or below the previous one (never above `requiredY`), re-running `messageFitsAt` per candidate and restoring every temporary move in a `finally`. The advertised set is the verified arrangement; `[]` when none holds.
  - `messageFitsAt` hardening, all driven by review findings: candidate geometry is read at the moved position with the memoized note layout invalidated (`noteLayouts.delete`), so a reached message with its own note is judged where it would actually land; a moved message's own note must still end above the content limit on an authored canvas (an automatic one regrows); and a position within 4 px of a segment frame edge is rejected (`sequence/segment-message-border-run`; the shared `composition/container-border-run` check keeps the exact-collinearity case covered in every profile).
  - The single-blocker path (`noteSingleAdjustment`) keeps its one-slot preference — `requiredY` first — and gains the same bounded step-over for an edge or near miss, capped by the next message the note does not reach (the reported timeline order is preserved; the unedited payment draft in `test/sequence-segment-labels.test.mjs` still advertises `[]`).
  - No cap truncates wide failures: the scan bound scales with the reached count (a 23-message chain yields 23 fixes `996…1612`).
- `test/sequence-note-wrap.test.mjs` — 29 tests: the 20 maintained note-wrap cases plus nine new ones covering the issue's joint adjustment (red on the pristine renderer: 20 pass / 9 fail), the ordered withhold when the arrangement would cross a later message or lack authored room, the moved-position geometry of a reached message's own note, the authored-canvas content limit, a segment frame edge (multi and single paths), disjoint lanes keeping a closer row (no forced uniform `+28`), and the long chain.

## Stability impact

- Impact class and changed behavior/shared callers: Shared behavior. `render-sequence.mjs` produces diagnostics for every sequence artifact through `validate`, `render`, `deliver`, and `compare`. Only the receipt contents of a failing `sequence/note-overlap` change (plus the repairs offered); passing documents and rendered SVG are byte-identical (`render sequence examples/cache-miss-request.sequence.json` is sha256 `89c56e9e…` on base and head).
- Existing behavior preserved / intended compatibility changes / failure behavior: human messages stay byte-identical except the new `and N more message(s) below` clause on multi-reached receipts; exit codes and the set of inputs that pass or fail are unchanged. Intended change: a multi-reached failure advertises the whole verified adjustment instead of one edit that reorders the timeline.

## Also repairs the tip's generated checks (#910 aftermath)

While verifying this branch on the tip, `npm run test:generated` fails there — reproduced on the pristine renderer before this branch's changes, and the same `test (22)` job is red on dev's own push run for `96234021` while its predecessor `d5806a6f` was green. #910 changed the shared HTML template and the three guide templates without re-deriving their downstream artifacts, so this PR carries the mechanical repair as its second commit:

- `check-release-identity` read the star icon's SVG path data (`l1.9 3.9 4.3.6-3.1`) as a hardcoded package version; the path numbers are now separated (`4.3 .6-3.1`), leaving the icon geometry identical while no longer matching the version pattern.
- All 15 bundled example renders under `examples/` and `archify/examples/`, plus the `examples/web-app.html` viewer example, are re-derived from their JSON IR (`npm --prefix archify run render:examples` plus the packaged render; `test/golden.mjs` re-checks all three template-owned artifacts); `npm run test:generated` now passes end to end.
- `archify.zip` is rebuilt from the re-derived tree; versus the previous build of this branch it differs only in its 15 packaged example members.
- The checked-in site pages and proofs are re-derived with the repository's own generators: `docs/guide.html` (`build-guide.mjs`), `docs/start.html` (`build-start.mjs`), `docs/gallery.html`, `docs/gallery/manifest.json` and the 12 gallery artifacts (`build-gallery.mjs docs`), `examples/checkout-platform-delta.html` and its receipt (`archify compare architecture` with the checked fixtures), and the README live-proof GIF plus receipt (`scripts/build-readme-showcase.mjs`, headless Chrome capture + ffmpeg, 54 frames / 5.4 s / 815,100 bytes). The five reproducibility tests — `guide-page`, `start-page`, `gallery`, the checkout case in `architecture-delta`, and `readme-showcase` — pass on the result.
- `published-update-manifest` stays red for a reason outside this diff: dev's `docs/skill-updates/archify/stable.json` still describes v3.0.1 while release v3.1.0 was published at 17:23Z. `release.yml` documents that manifest as a post-Release follow-up commit ("publish … in a follow-up commit"), and the failing job message asks for exactly that; it is deliberately left to the release flow.

## Tests run

Base `origin/dev` `96234021` → candidate head `61ee87fd` (sequence fix `14b4c7c1`, tip repair `54ccf00d`, artifact re-derivation `2ae106d0`, live-proof rebuild `61ee87fd`).

- New suite on the head: 29/29 pass. Red proof: the same test file on the pristine renderer (head tree with only the renderer reverted) scores 20 pass / 9 fail — exactly the nine new cases.
- Focused batch via the repository runner (`sequence-note-wrap`, `sequence-segment-labels`, `sequence-canvas-diagnostics`, `sequence-column-fit`, `sequence-header-clearance`, `sequence-self-message`, `sequence-width-review`, `render-failure-diagnostics`, `renderer-diagnostic-boundary`): 116 tests, 114 pass, 0 fail, 2 browser-gated skips — identical under Node 22.23.1 and Node 24.18.0.
- Repair-loop probe (6 fixtures: the issue, moved-position geometry, content limit, frame edge, disjoint lanes, 23-message chain): every advertised set applies to `exit 0` on revalidation, repeats are byte-identical.
- The issue's own fixture: the receipt now advertises `set /messages/1/y to 399` and `set /messages/2/y to 427`; applying both revalidates clean.
- Repo pins: `test/sequence-segment-labels.test.mjs` 21/21 including the unedited payment draft's `supportedFixes: []` (a follower the note does not reach pins the no-crossing rule).
- `npm run test:generated` on the head: release identity, all 30 example freshness checks, and version sync pass (`test/golden.mjs` exit 0); it fails on the pristine tip — see the `#910 aftermath` section. `scripts/package-smoke.mjs` passes on the extracted archive on win32.
- Full suite `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` on the head: 3141 tests, 2907 pass / 56 fail, against the baseline tree (dev renderer + dev tests) at 3132 / 2896 / 58. Comparing the two failure sets name-by-name (ignoring the Windows `EPERM` symlink skips that only differ by temp path), the head's only remaining extra is the README live-proof test that the fourth commit fixes, and the baseline's extras are the two tip-side reproducibility tests this branch restores (`gallery`, checkout-delta) plus one `update-notifier` timing flake that flips between runs (`cache startup…` this time, `two promoters…` before — both pass in isolation on the head). The nine new note-overlap tests are green throughout.

## Visual evidence

Not applicable — non-visual diagnostics and repair receipts change; rendered output is byte-identical.

## Generated artifacts

- `archify.zip` rebuilt with the canonical Node 22.23.1 toolchain (bundled zlib `1.3.1-e00f703`), reproducible byte-for-byte on a repeat build (`726e99ee…`, 5,019,507 bytes); calibrated against a pristine rebuild of this tip, from which it differs in the renderer plus the re-derived example members this PR refreshes for #910. The archive committed on `dev` (blob `00baeb4d5d`) predates #910's template/example changes entirely, so the rebuilt archive also refreshes its 7 stale members. `scripts/package-smoke.mjs` passes on the extracted archive on win32.

items.title: fix(architecture): prefer straight routes over unnecessary Port Spread doglegs
items.body:
## User problem

Fixes #137.

Architecture auto-routing preserved a conspicuous shallow dogleg for an unobstructed, near-aligned relationship whenever **both** endpoints participated in Automatic Port Spread. `alignFacingPorts()` returned the two independently selected spread slots unchanged, and the router then emitted an outside-channel bridge. With the shared 8px corner radius the result read as a small S-curve, i.e. routing noise, even though a straight segment was available.

## What changes

- `alignFacingPorts()` (architecture renderer) now treats the doubly-spread, near-aligned facing case as a joint port+route optimization instead of an unconditional early return.
- New `straightenSharedSpreadPorts()` tries an ordered, deterministic list of shared-axis coordinates (the relationship's own two spread slots first, then the component centers/midpoint) and accepts the first candidate that satisfies **all** existing gates: corner clearance, endpoint-side direction contract, endpoint-component clearance, and obstacle clearance — plus a new port-distinctness check.
- New `spreadPortIsDistinct()` ensures the chosen slot does not collapse onto a competing relationship's spread slot on the same component side (compared against the shared spread map, so the result is independent of connection input order).
- Regression test updated: the fixture from #137 now asserts a two-point straight route (`[[380,320],[380,160]]`), distinct competing ports, and stability under reversed connection input order. A horizontal (left/right) variant is added.

## What deliberately does not change

- Singly-spread and unspread alignment behavior is untouched.
- The blocked-axis case still routes around the obstacle via the outside bridge (the straightening candidate fails the obstacle-clearance check and falls back).
- Explicit authored geometry (`via`, named `route`, `channelX`/`channelY`, `labelAt`) still bypasses automatic alignment entirely.
- No schema, diagnostic-code, or CLI changes.

## Compatibility and migration impact

None. This only improves route selection for a specific automatic-routing configuration; authored geometry and validation rules are unchanged. Existing schema-v1 documents remain valid.

## Failure behavior and rollback path

If no compatible distinct axis exists (axis blocked, or every candidate would collide with a competing port or violate corner/side clearance), the function returns `null` and the previous outside-bridge route is preserved. Reverting the single commit restores the prior behavior.

## Evidence

- `node --test test/automatic-port-spread.test.mjs` — 16/16 pass (includes updated #137 fixture + new horizontal + reversed-order determinism checks).
- Full `npm test` in `archify/` (brand marks, validators, release identity, golden, and the full suite including showcase composition gates): **747 tests, 719 pass, 0 fail, 28 skipped** (skips are `ARCHIFY_CHROME` browser-only regressions).
- Rendered #137 fixture before/after:
  - before: `source-target -> 373,320;373,296;403,296;403,184;387,184;387,160` (6-point outside bridge)
  - after: `source-target -> 380,320;380,160` (straight), while `source-peer-target` and `source-target-peer` keep their distinct ports.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
  * Architecture connections now use straighter, zero-bend routes when ports are near-aligned and the shared path is unobstructed.
  * Port separation is preserved to prevent routing ambiguity.
  * Connections retain their outside route when the shared axis is blocked.
  * Routing results remain consistent regardless of input ordering.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

items.title: fix(sequence): repair multi-message note overlaps
items.body:
## Problem
A wrapped Sequence note can cover multiple later messages. The previous diagnostic suggested moving only the first blocker; applying that edit could leave the next blocker at the same required y with no executable follow-up repair.

Closes #903

## Value
The note-overlap diagnostic now provides an executable repair for a contiguous run of blocked messages, avoiding a repair dead end.

## Approach
- Project all later messages at or below the first blocker by the required offset while preserving their relative spacing.
- Offer the ordered compound edit only when every projected message remains inside the timeline and clear of messages, labels, routes, notes, and the wrapped note.
- Record the projected message paths and y coordinates in diagnostic evidence.
- Add a regression that applies the advertised compound edit and verifies `validate` succeeds.

## Validation
- `node --test --test-name-pattern="several messages" --test-reporter=spec test/sequence-note-wrap.test.mjs`
- `npm run test:generated`

## Impact
No schema changes. Existing single-blocker fixes retain their same `set /messages/<index>/y` form; a multi-blocker case now emits ordered semicolon-separated edits.

items.title: fix(workflow): offer a member-preserving group placement for blocked routes
items.body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

## Revision history

- **`c52a8ce` / `e2267b80` — first head.** Diagnostic evidence plus a group-placement repair.
- **`d6beaabe` — second head.** Addressed the first review finding.
- **`04f774eb` — current head.** Addresses the second review finding.

### Review finding addressed: the repair could be empty, or eject a member

[Codex](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/838#discussion_r) found two concrete defects in the first head's candidate search, which stepped `toCol` down by one from the authored span. Both reproduce:

| shape | first head | current head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| group spanning **exactly** the blocking column (`fromCol: 1, toCol: 1`) | `supportedFixes: []` — the loop tested only `0..0` and the unchanged `1..1`, never the `0..1` span that compiles | advertises `fromCol 0, toCol 1`, which compiles |
| wider group owning a node in its **rightmost** column | advertised a compiling span that **ejected that node** from the group | advertises `0..3`, keeping the member at column 3 inside the span |

The second one is the more serious: `acceptsFix` only proves the document compiles, so a span that silently drops a member still verified. The search now derives the members' own column range and only considers spans that contain it, so ejection is impossible by construction rather than by luck. `readableGroupBounds` already excludes nodes outside `fromCol..toCol`, which is what made the ejection silent.

Two regression cases cover both shapes and assert that the advertised span compiles **and** keeps every member. Reverting to the first head's search makes them fail (`pass 0 / fail 1`).

### Second review finding: the repair could absorb a node that was never in the group

Both [Codex](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/838#discussion_r4239894375) and [CodeRabbit](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/838#discussion_r4239894471) reported that the member filter matched **every** same-lane node with an integer `col`, never consulting the group's own span. An unrelated same-lane node outside `fromCol..toCol` therefore looked like a member and stretched the advertised span to reach it:

```text
fixture + unrelated "responders" node at col 5
  first head -> advertised 0..5, absorbing the col-5 node, although 0..1 compiles
  current    -> advertised 0..1, col-5 node stays outside
```

That overreached *and* silently changed the unrelated node's context while claiming to keep members. The filter is now bounded by the authored span, which enforces the reviewer's suggested check by construction rather than re-testing each candidate: `minimumFrom` cannot drop below the lowest genuine member, `maximumTo` cannot rise above the highest, and the enumeration stays inside `group.toCol`.

A third regression case covers this shape and asserts the real member stays inside the span while the unrelated node stays outside. Reverting the filter makes it fail. The earlier two cases still pass.

### Third review round: a test that could not fail, and a shape with no repair

Two further findings, both addressed or answered:

- **[CodeRabbit](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/838#discussion_r4239908689): one added assertion compiled a hard-coded span.** The first test applied `0..2` literally instead of the advertised span, so it could pass while the diagnostic offered something else. It now parses the advertised `fromCol`/`toCol` and applies those, as the two sibling tests already did — all three validate the repair actually offered to the user.
- **[Codex](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/838#discussion_r4239908622): adding an unrelated node at col 0 to the single-column fixture still absorbs it.** Verified, and deliberately left unfixed. Every span that keeps the col-1 member also contains col 0, so no member-preserving repair exists for that shape; the search correctly returns no suggestion. Absorption here is also deliberate group semantics, not a side effect of the repair: `nodeContext()` derives membership from the column range, and the validator only requires a group to contain *some* node. Advertising such a span would be exactly the silent context change the finding objects to, so the code reports nothing instead. No change to group membership semantics was made.

### Fourth review round: a false repair I had argued was acceptable

[BlueboxC](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/issues/821#issuecomment-6194631942) independently ported this change and added a **membership-equality** check that this branch was missing. Verified against head `18c8e0ba`, the missing check was a real false repair:

```text
unrelated node at col 0 (left of the authored span)
   advertised: 0..1
   membership preserved? false
```

My earlier reply on that thread argued this shape had no repairable span and that returning nothing was therefore honest. The conclusion was right; the implementation did not reach it correctly. The filter limited which nodes could *derive* the span, but nothing rejected a **candidate** whose span moved the membership of same-lane nodes outside the authored range — so the repair shipped with a message claiming it "keeps its members" while doing the opposite.

The invariant is now explicit, adopted from that port:

```js
const movesMembership = asArray(workflow.nodes).some((node) => node.lane === group.lane
  && (node.col >= fromCol && node.col <= toCol)
    !== (node.col >= group.fromCol && node.col <= group.toCol));
if (movesMembership) continue;
```

This is the compiler's own notion of membership — `nodeContext()` selects a group by column range — so "unchanged membership" is the correct requirement rather than a stricter one.

| input | before | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unrelated node at col 0 | advertised `0..1`, membership changed | **no repair**, `blockedBy` still reported |
| no extra nodes / col 3 / col 5 | `0..1` | `0..1` (unchanged) |

Four regression cases now cover the repair: single-column group, rightmost-column member, span-outside node, and the withheld case (which asserts that any advertised span leaves membership identical to the authored one). Reverting the guard fails it. Credit to BlueboxC in the commit message and the thread.

### Fifth review round: overlapping groups reorder the resolved context

[Codex](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/838#discussion_r4284487287) found a further gap after the membership guard: with two **overlapping** groups in one lane, moving the edited group's `fromCol` can reorder them.

```text
command 1..1 overlapping other 0..1, same lane
  advertised: 0..1
  BEFORE: col-1 node resolves to: Other
  AFTER : col-1 node resolves to: Incident command
  RESOLUTION CHANGED? true
```

`nodeContext()` takes the first group whose range contains the node, with groups ordered by lane, then `fromCol`, then `toCol`, then `id`. Lowering `command.fromCol` to 0 sorts it ahead of `other`, so it takes over the node — while the edited group's own node set is unchanged, which is why the membership check could not see it.

The guard now compares the **resolved group per node** on both sides of the edit rather than membership, which subsumes the earlier check. Three of the five regression cases assert that **no** repair is offered, which is the honest answer whenever no span preserves context:

| input | advertised |
| --- | --- |
| overlapping groups | **none** |
| node immediately left of the span | **none** |
| node outside the span on the right | `0..1` |
| no extra nodes / plain fixture | `0..1` |

## Problem and value

Fixes #821.

A `workflow/route-preset-conflict` raised because a **scene label** blocks the only column an authored endpoint side can use currently publishes an empty `supportedFixes`:

```json
{
  "code": "workflow/route-preset-conflict",
  "message": "Workflow edge \"alert->page\" cannot satisfy route preset \"drop\": candidate violates lane/phase/group label clearance.",
  "supportedFixes": []
}
```

That is not an oversight in the existing search — it exhausts honestly. Instrumenting the rejection shows the blocker is a specific group label:

```text
BLOCKED-BY-SEGMENT seg=2
  obstacle = {"kind":"group-label","id":"command","x":174,"y":202,"width":89.6,"height":14}
  route    = [[94,145],[94,166],[214,166],[214,217]]
```

Segment 2 is the final vertical approach into the target node's **top** edge, and the group label `"Incident command"` spans exactly that column. Three consequences follow, all measured on `dev` @ `0b8f9f34`:

| authored change | result |
| --- | --- |
| `route` set to each of the other five presets | **all fail** (`orthogonal non-zero segments`, `perpendicular endpoint-side direction`) |
| `route` removed | fails as `workflow/explicit-pin-conflict` |
| every `fromSide`/`toSide` pairing | **all fail** |
| `page.width` widened to 132 | fails, same invariant |
| all lane labels shortened | fails, same invariant |
| **group `fromCol`/`toCol` narrowed off the target column** | **compiles** |
| group removed | compiles |
| target node moved to another column | compiles |

So no route-side repair exists, and the only authored field that does repair the document is the group's own placement. Meanwhile the enumeration *does* find a scene-clear route (`[[94,145],[764,145],[764,217],[214,217]]`) but correctly refuses it because it is an `outside-right` shape, not the authored `drop` preset family.

Value: the reporter of #821 — and two of the repository's own bundled v1 examples plus one baseline fixture, which cannot complete `migrate --to-schema 2` — currently receives an unactionable dead end. This change makes the failure self-repairing without touching how routes or labels are placed.

## Stability impact

- **Impact class:** Local behavior — one diagnostic path in the readable-v2 compiler (`CONTRIBUTING.md#choose-evidence-by-impact`). No layout, routing, clearance or geometry change; the same documents that compiled before compile now, and the same ones fail.
- **Changed behavior, two parts:**
  1. `workflow/route-preset-conflict` for the `lane/phase/group label clearance` invariant now carries **evidence**: `segmentIndex` and `blockedBy: { kind, id }`. This mirrors the existing evidence the same diagnostic already publishes for other invariants (`obstacleNode`, `labelRect`, `segmentIndex`, `actualSegmentPx`/`requiredSegmentPx`).
  2. When the blocker is a `group-label`, the diagnostic advertises the group placement that **verifies**, using the existing `verifiedEdgeFix`/`acceptsFix` machinery — the same mechanism that already gates the route-preset and label-segment repairs, so an unverified suggestion still cannot be published.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** when no repair verifies, `supportedFixes` stays empty exactly as before. The two existing tests that assert an empty `supportedFixes` array are for the `workflow/solver-budget-exhausted` and `explicit label-label clearance` invariants, which this change does not touch — both still pass.
- **Scope boundary, deliberately:** only `group-label` blockers are repaired. A `lane-header` or `phase-header` blocker needs different authored fields and is left to the existing behaviour rather than guessed at.
- **Compatibility / failure behavior:** no schema, default, exit-code or receipt-shape change. The diagnostic keeps its stable `code`, and the failure still exits non-zero.
- **Generated artifacts:** `archify.zip` **is** affected. `archify/renderers/workflow/workflow-compiler.mjs` is packaged, and `scripts/ci-scope.mjs` does not match that path to a renderer/shared rule, so it falls through to `requireFull = true` and the `package` gate runs (the first CI run confirmed this: `zip-freshness` failed). The archive is refreshed in a follow-up commit — see below.

## Tests run

Comparison base `upstream/dev` @ `8072d6a2`; candidate head `68cb7418` (rebased onto current `dev` @ `8072d6a2`).

```sh
# Focused
node scripts/run-tests.mjs test/workflow-compiler-hard-contract.test.mjs
node scripts/run-tests.mjs test/workflow-migration.test.mjs
node scripts/run-tests.mjs test/workflow-vertical-label.test.mjs
node scripts/run-tests.mjs test/workflow-placed-label-evidence.test.mjs

# Regression proof: source fix reverted, new test kept
git checkout -- archify/renderers/workflow/workflow-compiler.mjs
node scripts/run-tests.mjs test/workflow-compiler-hard-contract.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='group label blocking'

# Full suite
npm run test:full
```

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Regression proof (fix reverted, test kept) | ✖ **fail 1** — the new test's `evidence.blockedBy` assertion fails |
| With the fix | ✔ passes |
| `test/workflow-compiler-hard-contract.test.mjs` (final head) | ✔ tests 103 / pass 103 / fail 0 |
| Review regression proof: source reverted to the first head's search | ✖ **fail 1** — the member-preserving test catches it |
| Review regression proof: member filter reverted | ✖ **fail 1** — the absorption test catches it |
| Review regression proof: membership guard reverted | ✖ **fail 1** — the withheld-repair test catches it |
| Review regression proof: context guard reverted | ✖ **fail 1** — the overlapping-group test catches it |
| `npm run test:full` (Chromium provided, final head) | ℹ tests 3527 / pass 3500 / fail 0 / cancelled 0 / skipped 27 / todo 0 — **exit 0** |

A pristine `upstream/dev` @ `0b8f9f34` checkout was measured beforehand for comparison: `tests 3235 / pass 3217 / fail 0 / skipped 18`. The candidate adds exactly three passing tests and introduces no failure.

The new regression test asserts the whole contract, not just the string: the invariant and `blockedBy` evidence, that **no** route-preset or route-removal fix is advertised for this shape, that the advertised group placement is present, and that **applying it compiles** (`ok: true`). Verifying the published fix independently outside the test — setting `groups[0].fromCol = 0`, `toCol = 2` — yields `ok=true` and a 786,517-byte render.

**Coverage gap, stated honestly:** the browser gate is exercised locally with a Chromium-based browser (Microsoft Edge) rather than Google Chrome, because Chrome is not installed on this host. This change is compiler-only and touches no Viewer/browser behaviour, so browser identity is not material to it; the full-suite run is done with Chromium available so the browser-conditional cases execute instead of skipping.

## Visual evidence

Not applicable — diagnostic payload and repair discovery only; no rendered geometry changes.

## Generated artifacts

`archify.zip` is affected and was rebuilt in a follow-up commit, from the committed source, with the canonical toolchain (official Node **22.23.2**, bundled zlib **1.3.1-e00f703**; confirmed via `node -p 'process.versions.zlib'`).

- The same toolchain reproduces the **pristine `dev` archive byte-identically**, which validates both the toolchain and the comparison base before regenerating.
- The rebuild is deterministic (two consecutive builds byte-identical).
- Comparing archives entry by entry, the **only** entry whose bytes differ is `archify/renderers/workflow/workflow-compiler.mjs`; the embedded copy matches `git show HEAD:archify/renderers/workflow/workflow-compiler.mjs` exactly.
- The `zip-freshness` gate was simulated locally (`scripts/build-zip.sh` + `cmp`) and passes.

No other generated output is affected.

## Release follow-up

None — no version, tag, manifest, or distribution identity change.

Fixes #821

items.title: docs(website): add a source-backed MCO runtime case study
items.body:

items.title: fix(dataflow): report the vertical-extent repair contract with measured bounds
items.body:
Addresses the data-flow half of #468. The lifecycle half of the earlier revision is superseded by the v3 redesign (`1dff447 feat(lifecycle)!`), so the lifecycle renderer and README are unchanged from `dev`.

## Problem and value

The data-flow vertical check used to fail with one generic `layout/constraint` diagnostic whose only guidance was the free-text hint `(adjust row/yOffset or increase meta.viewBox[1])`, with an empty `supportedFixes`. Both halves of that hint could be followed exactly and still fail:

- `keep y between 104 and 446` ignored the node's height, so a node whose bottom crossed the bound stayed broken after the advised move;
- raising `meta.viewBox[1]` clears the layout check, but the canvas is also the reader's page; without a page-fit check the raise can push the delivered artifact past 1440×900 and fail `visual-check` one command later.

The renderer now reports `dataflow/node-above-area` and `dataflow/node-below-area` independently — the renderer's native `diagnostics` pattern (`{ code, severity, message, subject, evidence, supportedFixes }` entries passed alongside the message strings), matching `dataflow/unknown-endpoint` and the v3 lifecycle renderer — each with the node as `subject`, measured evidence, and an ordered repair list:

| before | after |
| --- | --- |
| one `layout/constraint` diagnostic | `dataflow/node-above-area` / `dataflow/node-below-area`, reported independently |
| `supportedFixes: []` | ordered repairs, each verified to clear the bound it is attached to |
| free-text hint | measured evidence: `y`, `height`, the area bounds, `requiredViewBoxHeight`, `requiredViewBoxFitsViewport`, `maximumViewBoxHeight`, and the predicted page height when the raise cannot fit |
| `keep y between 104 and 446` | `keep y within [104, 388] so that y + height does not pass 446` |
| "increase meta.viewBox[1]" (unbounded) | `raise meta.viewBox[1] to at least 602 and at most 606` |

The canvas raise is evaluated with the same `predictedFixedWidthOverflow` math `check-render-output` applies for `composition/viewport-height`: a data-flow canvas with an authored `meta.viewBox` gets no readable-scroll exception (`references/delivery-contract.md`: "explicit viewBoxes in other modes … remain failures"), so the raise is offered as a standalone repair only while the raised page still fits. The range's lower end clears the node; the upper end is `floor(width / 1.55)` — the wide-reader ratio, above which the reader can still narrow the page. When the raise cannot fit, it is not offered, the message carries the predicted page height, and only the compaction repairs remain. When no single change clears a bound, the message says so and names the pair that does.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: failure diagnostics and repair text only. Rendered SVG output, geometry, and layout are unchanged (`golden.mjs` passes).
- Shared callers: none — the change is local to `archify/renderers/dataflow/render-dataflow.mjs`; `predictedFixedWidthOverflow` and `DECLARED_WIDE_READER_RATIO` are consumed from `renderers/shared/desktop-readability.mjs` unchanged.
- Failure behavior: pass/fail outcomes are unchanged; failing specs get typed diagnostics instead of the generic one.

## Tests run

- Comparison base `dev` `9ef0961`, head `c31437b` (single commit; rebased 2026-10-08 onto the current `dev` — the renderer auto-merged with upstream's dataflow work and `archify.zip` was rebuilt).
- `node --test test/vertical-extent-repair.test.mjs` — 9/9: both bounds independently (codes, subjects, evidence values, message bounds), the dual-bound case, the schema-minimum guard, each offered fix applied and asserted to clear its diagnostic, both sides of the viewport-fit gate, the bounded raise range and its single-value equality form, the three-entry repair order, the height cap inside the area with its paired y-range, and the no-single-change case (message names the pair).
- Focused batch (`vertical-extent-repair`, `dataflow-automatic-layout`, `render-failure-diagnostics`, `renderer-diagnostic-boundary`) — 65/65.
- Repository suite (`node scripts/run-tests.mjs`, Node 22.23.1 / zlib 1.3.1-e00f703): 2574 tests, 2361 pass, 150 skipped, 63 fail. This Windows machine fails a fixed set of environment-dependent tests (symlink/hard-link privilege, and Windows path separators in the runner tests); the failure set on this head is byte-identical to a pristine `dev` checkout's. (That comparison was measured on the pre-rebase head; on the rebased head the focused suite is 9/9, the same suite is 9/9 red on a pristine current-`dev` checkout with only the test file applied, the adjacent `dataflow-automatic-layout` / `render-failure-diagnostics` / `renderer-diagnostic-boundary` batch is 63/63, and `golden` plus the four generator/identity checks pass. CI runs the full suite on this head.) `node test/golden.mjs` passes, and so do the four generator/identity checks (`check:viewer`, `check:brand-marks`, `check:validators`, `check:release-identity`).

## Visual evidence

Evidence branch `evidence/485-dataflow-repair` (screenshots and receipts; fork only).

- **The raise that fits** — the diagnostic offers `raise meta.viewBox[1] to at least 602 and at most 606` (`requiredViewBoxFitsViewport: true`). Applied at 602: `validate` ok, `deliver` ok, `browser-check` pass at 1440×900 / 1600×1000 / 1920×1080 / 2048×1320 light and 1440×900 dark, `visual-check` pass. At 1440×900 the page composition is 12 body + 52 header + 78 diagram chrome + 746 SVG = 888px (no scroll), reader width 1195, minimum projected node text 7px / edge labels 8px. [1440×900 screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gold-beyond/archify/evidence/485-dataflow-repair/evidence/dataflow-repair-raised-1440x900.png)
- **The compaction repair** — `lower yOffset on node "audit"` (to −180): same chain, all pass. [1440×900 screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gold-beyond/archify/evidence/485-dataflow-repair/evidence/dataflow-repair-compacted-1440x900.png)
- **The raise the tool refuses to recommend** — the same fixture with a 156px-tall node: `requiredViewBoxHeight: 700` (above the 606 ceiling at this width), `requiredViewBoxFitsViewport: false`, predicted page ≈1128px. Raising anyway to 700 clears `validate` but fails `browser-check` with `viewer/viewport-overflow` at 1440×900 light (scrollHeight 1150), 1600×1000 (1274), 1920×1080 (1274) and 1440×900 dark; 2048×1320 light passes. That is the trap the gate exists to avoid. [Receipt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gold-beyond/archify/evidence/485-dataflow-repair/evidence/case-b-raised.browser-check.json)
- Comparison conditions: same fixture, canvas, 1440×900 light viewport, and preset; raised vs compacted repairs.
- Automated/browser checks: as above. Perceptual review: author-inspected captures only — the automated receipts record `visualReview: pending`, and the two screenshots were inspected to show the complete diagram and viewer chrome inside the viewport.

## Generated artifacts

- Regenerated `archify.zip` (contains the renderer change); a clean rebuild is `cmp`-identical, `sha256 7e7343d771301907687714e8889757f69b209bcbd73fceeb63dcf38ae06723d9`.
- `assets/template.html`, gallery, examples, and validators are unchanged — no rendered-output change.

## Scope / tradeoffs

- The repair list keeps only entries that clear the bound on their own. `lower yOffset` moves the whole node and is offered only while the node fits between the bounds; `reduce height` moves only the bottom edge and is offered only while a legal height (schema minimum 36) reaches the bound at the node's current y.
- The raise is offered against the canvas the author ships, not against the current file: authoring `meta.viewBox` at all removes the automatic `intrinsic-height` declaration, so the raise is a real tradeoff — the diagnostic states the measured consequence instead of leaving it as prose.
- Not changed: the horizontal bounds keep their current untyped messages; widening-plus-raising to keep the ratio above the wide threshold would pass the gate by padding empty air, which is not offered.

## Problem and value

Lifecycle diagrams generated from real repositories (dev @ `64da9d39`, 6 user projects) looked tangled, and in every one the runtime "来源 N" source badge sat on the state's type sigil or label at a 5.5px, 76%-opacity size that was hard to read. Root causes, verified in `render-lifecycle.mjs`:

1. Lower bands used a different column grid (event/terminal `col N` = main `col N + 2`), so an interruption could never sit under the main state it leaves. Its routes crossed the canvas.
2. Fixed 118px states on a 154px pitch left 36px gaps: too narrow for a reciprocal pair plus labels. The 980px canvas also left its right third empty.
3. The implied phase rail doubled authored main transitions.
4. Lifecycle put its sigil top-right (every other mode puts it top-left), exactly where the viewer places the source badge. Label layout reserved no room for the badge.
5. In the legend, decision and failure shared the same red, and start and terminal states were told apart only by color.

Changing column semantics or geometry would reinterpret authored v1 IR. Following the workflow precedent in `schemas/README.md`, the layout ships as **lifecycle `schema_version: 2`**. v1 files keep their exact state geometry.

## Stability impact

- **Impact class:** renderer layout plus a shared presentation change.
  - Lifecycle v2: new `grid-routing.mjs`, and a v2 branch in `render-lifecycle.mjs`.
  - Shared:
    - `nodeLabelLayout` gains a `source` reservation, used by lifecycle, data-flow, and workflow.
    - `placeAutomaticLabels` gains an opt-in `gridSweep`. The architecture path is unchanged.
    - The viewer source badge moves and restyles.
    - `SIGIL_TONE` maps active→cyan, success→green, and decision→purple. This recolors those node icons in any mode.
- **v2:**
  - Layout:
    - One row per populated lane: `main` first, `terminal` last. Row titles are vertical in the left gutter.
    - One shared `col` 0–4 grid.
    - Column gaps widen for labels on same-row neighbour transitions, capped by the desktop readability budget of the smallest state text.
    - Row gaps open for the tracks their routes need. The canvas is sized automatically.
    - State text is one step larger.
  - Routing: an orthogonal grid router.
    - Reciprocal pairs run as parallel lines.
    - Tracks in each gap are ordered to minimize crossings, and collinear overlaps are nudged apart.
    - Blocked descents use the corridor between columns. Unlabelled edges in an outer column loop around the grid.
    - The implied rail is removed. A forward main transition with no `variant` renders as the emphasized primary path.
  - Labels: showcase labels are ranked beside their line, then on it, then outward past parallels. They prefer the side away from a reciprocal neighbour.
- **Both versions (presentation only):**
  - Sigil moves top-left; the brand stays top-right.
  - Start states get a UML initial marker. States without outgoing transitions get a double border.
  - The legend shows the start marker plus a non-interactive `final` entry, which disappears when every kind entry is hidden.
  - Empty v1 band titles are hidden.
- **Schema:**
  - `schema_version` becomes `enum [1, 2]`, and generated validators are regenerated.
  - The `viewBox` height minimum drops to 300 so an auto-sized v2 canvas stays expressible. The v1 renderer still requires 566, so v1 acceptance is unchanged.
- **Preserved:**
  - v1 state rects are byte-identical; there is a test for this.
  - `meta.legend.entries` keys, focus/relationship semantics, and source-evidence links are unchanged.
  - All six real v1 candidates still pass `finalize --quality showcase`.
- **Docs:** `SKILL.md` keeps pointing at `deployment-release.lifecycle.json`, which is now v2 with explicit main-path transitions and an `approved` recovery edge. `agent-run.lifecycle.json` stays v1. Authoring defaults, the authoring contract, the lifecycle README, the schema policy, the CHANGELOG, and 8 locale catalogs are updated.
- **Known limitation:** a very dense diagram can leave a label with no clear spot. Example: 9 labelled transitions on 6 states, where four lines share one bottom side. `finalize` then fails with `composition/label-route-clearance`, and the existing bounded repair applies. In the SOMO case, shortening one label passes.

## Tests run

Base `64da9d39` (origin/dev), head `e1eab5c8`, official Node 22.23.2 (zlib 1.3.1-e00f703):

- `npm test`: 2273 pass, 0 fail, 85 skipped (includes the golden, viewer, validator, and zip freshness checks)
- `npm run test:browser` (Chrome): 270 pass, 0 fail
- `npm run test:webm`: 7 pass, 0 fail
- New `test/lifecycle-v2-layout.test.mjs`:
  - showcase validation
  - shared column grid and populated-only row titles
  - canvas width
  - no rail, plus primary-path emphasis
  - orthogonal routes and parallel reciprocal pairs
  - initial and final marks
  - `nodeLabelLayout` source reservation
  - v1 geometry freeze
- `repository-evidence-types-browser.test.mjs` asserts that the badge bbox does not intersect the sigil, brand, or label. This covers workflow, sequence, data-flow, v1 lifecycle, and v2 lifecycle with a brand.
- Updated expectations:
  - `legend-contract` / `webm` smoke (structural `final` entry)
  - `brand-marks` (badge offset 22)
  - `authoring-safety-contract` (lifecycle v1/v2 policy)
  - `edge-label-color` (v2 example coordinates)
  - `v1-compatibility` (9 legend entries)
- Fuzz, not committed: 200 random dense v2 diagrams with 3–4 lanes and roughly 1–2 edges per state. 199 pass showcase validation; the one failure is `label-route-clearance`. No crashes.

## Visual evidence

- **Evidence:** same candidate JSON, rendered by base (v1) and by head (converted to v2 the way the new guidance directs: columns under the source state, no pinned geometry). There are six real user lifecycles: SOMO, Hive dispatch, MDTU, interview, project-question, and Mobi. There is also the v2 `deployment-release` example.
  - Intended differences:
    - aligned rows
    - straight vertical exits
    - parallel reciprocal pairs
    - no doubled rail
    - readable badge left of the brand
    - UML marks
    - distinct decision color
  - Unexpected differences: none observed.
- **Comparison conditions:** 1440×900, light theme, default preset (the example uses its authored signal-flow preset), default page state and zoom.
- **Automated checks:** every v2 case passes `finalize --quality showcase` (validate, deliver, check, browser-check), except SOMO before the one-label repair noted above.
  - `resolvedCrossovers`: Mobi 6 → 2, interview 2 → 2, SOMO 4 → 5 after the repair (denser labelled topology). The other cases have none.
  - `routesOverSuggestedBends`: Hive 2 → 0, MDTU 1 → 0.
- **Perceptual visual review:** passed for Hive, MDTU, project-question, Mobi, interview, and the example. SOMO is improved but still busy because of its content density.

## Generated artifacts

Regenerated from the final source:
- `archify/assets/template.html`
- the `archify/examples/*.html` and `examples/*.html` goldens
- `examples/web-app.html` template blocks
- `examples/checkout-platform-delta.{html,receipt.json}`
- `docs/gallery.html`, `docs/gallery/**`
- `docs/cases/mco-runtime.architecture.html` and `experiments/mco-showcase/mco-runtime.html` (pinned MCO checkout)
- `docs/assets/archify-live-proof.{gif,json}`
- `archify/renderers/shared/generated-validators.mjs`
- `archify.zip` (official Node 22, byte-stable across rebuilds)

`docs/assets/archify-lifecycle.png` (README screenshot) is not regenerated here; it still shows the v1 look.

items.title: feat(lifecycle)!: lay out state machines from a main path
items.body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

## Problem and value

Six real-project lifecycle diagrams (Hive, MCO, Idea Finder; main and dev) all passed delivery on first finalize, yet read poorly. Every one showed the same problems:
- Transition labels floating far from their lines.
- Routes leaving card bottoms in parallel bundles, then taking long detours.
- Large empty areas forced by one-row-per-lane and shared columns.
- An author duplicating a terminal state (two `cancelled` nodes) to get around the grid router.

The cause is the model, not individual bugs: authors place states on a lane/column grid and a general-purpose orthogonal router connects them. Real lifecycles share one shape instead: a normal path, exits to terminal states (often from several phases), and loops back.

Schema v3 encodes that shape and the renderer derives every coordinate:
- **Main path:** `mainPath` lists the normal path in order; it renders as one left-to-right row with a label in each gap.
- **Back or skip transitions** along the main path: nested arcs above the row, with ordered ports so they don't cross.
- **Other states:** one depth row below per step away from the main path, under the state they branch from. Adjacent lower states connect side to side; other routes use tracks below.
- **One exit from several phases:** contiguous phases get a dashed group frame with one arrow (UML superstate); non-contiguous phases share one junction bus. No more fan-in or duplicate states.
- **Labels:** placed against their own route and kept clear of states, routes and other labels; if one can't be placed, spacing grows and layout reruns.

The renderer is 1,082 lines and replaces `render-lifecycle.mjs` plus `grid-routing.mjs` (1,387 lines). Authors no longer pick coordinates or route controls.

Once this lands, #623 and #244 (old routing/rail bugs) no longer apply, and #94 (Mermaid `stateDiagram` import) can map onto `mainPath`.

## Stability impact

- **Impact class: lifecycle renderer and schema replacement plus a shared checker change.**
- **Lifecycle:** the schema accepts only v3; v1/v2 inputs fail validation. No compatibility or migration path is kept on purpose: users describe diagrams to an Agent, which authors fresh JSON from the current schema each time, so there are no maintained v1/v2 sources to carry forward. Already-generated HTML is unaffected.
- **Shared checker (`geometry.mjs`, `check-render-output.mjs`):** routes that declare the same `data-composition-junction` may share its horizontal bus, a common source-port first tick, and the merged drop/arrowhead into the same target. Internal vertical overlap and overlap with unrelated routes still count. Only the lifecycle renderer emits this attribute today.
- **Not changed:** dead lifecycle-rail rules remain in `viewer/viewer.css`; removing them changes the viewer template and regenerates about 50 unrelated pages. Separate cleanup.

## Tests run

Base `dev@7112cc6d`, candidate `75ab88c3`. `524c577a` and `75ab88c3` (corner sigils, see below) was checked with `lifecycle-layout`, `node-icons`, `brand-marks`, `label-clearance`, `animation` and `generate-validators` (75/75), golden checks, validator freshness, the artifact checker on all ten lifecycle inputs, and an extracted-ZIP validate of both examples. Before that, `dc2edbd4` (visual pass, see below) was checked with `lifecycle-layout`, `layout-rules`, `legend-contract`, `label-clearance` (144/144), golden checks, three reader browser files in Chrome (`desktop-reader`, `repository-evidence-types`, `reader-layout`: 26/26), the artifact checker on all ten lifecycle inputs, and an extracted-ZIP validate of both examples. Earlier runs: The runs below were on `4e263f7e`; `b3a36875` only removes v1/v2 migration text, the two old-version rejection tests and the v1 lifecycle fixture, then regenerates validators and the ZIP. After it, `test/lifecycle-layout.test.mjs` and `test/v1-compatibility.test.mjs` pass (18/18) and validator freshness passes. `a6f86a0b` only restores the three website job-search files to the base revision.

- Old v1/v2-only lifecycle tests and fixtures are deleted (5 files, planner fixtures, the v1 lifecycle baseline). `test/lifecycle-layout.test.mjs` (7 tests) is added. Lifecycle cases in shared tests are moved to v3.
- All non-browser test files that mention lifecycle: 972 passed, 34 skipped, **4 failed**. The 4 failures are architecture output-limit tests in `cli.test.mjs`. They are timing-sensitive under parallel runs; clean `dev` and this branch both pass them 3/3 in isolation. So that run was not fully green.
- 14 browser test files that mention lifecycle, real Chrome: all pass.
- Golden checks and generated-validator freshness: pass.
- Full `npm test`, `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:webm` were **not** run locally; relying on this PR's CI for full coverage.

## Visual evidence

**Visual pass (`dc2edbd4`).** After an independent review of all ten renders, three visible problems were fixed: connectors jogged when a straight drop was possible (ports now try both partner-facing and even placement per spacing round and keep the placed layout with fewer bends; MCO dev has no bends, mco-main's one crossing is gone), transition labels were 9px next to 12px state names (now 10px, notes 9px), and the dashed composite frame blended with dashed transitions (now a faint dotted line; corners round at 12px). Not done: a dedicated bottom row for terminal states, which needs connectors that cross intermediate rows.

**Corner sigils (`524c577a`).** Every state had a corner sigil, so none stood out, and some misled: `decision` had no shape and fell back to the neutral square, the start state repeated the initial marker, and the active pulse read as health monitoring. Now `start`, `active` and `neutral` states get no default sigil; `waiting`, `decision` (new diamond), `success`, `failure` and `external` keep one. `icon` still overrides or hides any sigil, and `decision` joins the shared `nodeIcon` enum. No other renderer has a decision type, so no other artifacts change. Shared tests that assumed one sigil per lifecycle node now author an icon or count only sigil-bearing states.

A final `start`, `active` or `neutral` state is still an outcome, so it gets a new `stop` sigil (circle with a filled square; also an authored `icon`). With check and cross, every ending now carries a mark: in deployment-release, Aborted gains it. The state `type` schema now describes each type, and the lifecycle authoring contract explains how to choose one and how a Mermaid `stateDiagram` maps onto v3 (`[*]`, `<<choice>>`, composite states flattened with a shared exit, concurrent regions drawn as separate lifecycles).

- **README image:** [before (dev)](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/7112cc6d/docs/assets/archify-lifecycle.png) / [after](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/4e263f7e/docs/assets/archify-lifecycle.png).
- **Website:** unchanged. The job-search showcase (`docs/assets/life/job-search.lifecycle.webp`, `docs/cases/life/job-search.lifecycle.{html,json}`) stays at the base revision on purpose; its JSON is the old format and is not maintained as a v3 source. `docs/assets/archify-lifecycle.png` is shared by the README and the website home page, so that one image does change there.
- **Gallery:** `docs/gallery/artifacts/agent-run.lifecycle.html` and `deployment-release.lifecycle.html`. The deployment example now has an "abort" exit to show the group frame.
- **Real-project inputs:** the six inputs were converted to v3 by hand, choosing the main path for each. They are private and not attached. All pass the `showcase` artifact check:

| Input | Crossings |
|---|---|
| hive-dev, hive-main, idea-dev, idea-main, mco-dev, mco-main | 0 (mco-main had 1 before `dc2edbd4`) |
| Synthetic stress case (6-phase path, self-loop, nested loops, a shared exit spanning another phase's detour) | 4, halo-resolved |
| Bundled agent-run, deployment-release | 0 |

- **Automated or browser checks:** artifact checks above plus lifecycle browser tests.
- **Perceptual visual review:** author review only, at 1440 width; maintainer review pending. The five halo-resolved crossings and the new README and website images need a look.

## Generated artifacts

Rebuilt from the v3 sources in the second commit:
- `archify/examples/lifecycle-agent-run.html`, `examples/lifecycle-agent-run.html`
- `docs/gallery/artifacts/*.lifecycle.html`, `docs/gallery/manifest.json`, `docs/gallery.html`
- `docs/assets/archify-lifecycle.png`
- `archify/renderers/shared/generated-validators.mjs`
- `archify.zip`: official Node 22.23.2, bundled zlib `1.3.1-e00f703`. Two builds were byte-identical, and both lifecycle examples validate from the extracted package.

Guide and start pages are unaffected; the viewer template is unchanged, so other artifacts stay fresh.

Generated with [Devin](https://devin.ai)






### Review fixes (`b43bf56c`)
- Removed the stale `Versions 1 and 2 were removed` assertion that failed CI (`authoring-safety-contract`).
- Parallel transitions between neighbouring lower states now spread symmetrically (step `min(20, 48/(n-1))`; reciprocal pair unchanged at ±10). Three or more ride their labels on the line; more than five raise `lifecycle/crowded-side-transitions`.
- Shared exits merge into a frame/bus only when label, note and variant all match; otherwise each exit keeps its own route and label. Joined `a / b` labels are gone. hive-dev, mco-dev and mco-main change accordingly.
- Lifecycle routes opt into the shared-endpoint corridor and arrowhead checks (`data-composition-independent`); relations on one junction ending at the same state may share the merged drop and arrowhead. A mutated identical-route fixture now fails with `composition/ambiguous-corridor`.
- Evidence: narrow suite 358/358; all 10 representative inputs plus 3 repros pass `check`; golden, validators, viewer and gallery freshness pass; ZIP built twice with Node 22.23.2, identical sha256. README image unchanged (agent-run geometry identical).


### Maintainer boundary fixes (`344f4add`, archive `b2eedd55`)

#### Summary

```diff
- Five parallel labels or four label+note transitions exhaust the fixed side spacing.
+ Reserve each label footprint and enlarge only the affected lower row.
- A multi-target bus fails the corridor gate on its shared source tick.
+ Exempt only the common source-port first segment within the same junction.
```

The main path retains its height, every state within one lower row shares its centre and bottom, and subsequent rows/loop tracks follow the enlarged row. The two-direction pair remains at ±10; more than five transitions still fail with a typed diagnostic. The shared checker continues to reject different ports/junctions, disconnected subpaths and interior vertical overlaps.

#### Evidence

- **Before (`b43bf56c`):** five single-character transition labels and four labels with notes fail with `lifecycle/label-unplaced`; a five-state, two-target shared bus fails `validate`/`finalize` on two 34px source ticks.
  **After:** all three public repros pass. The bus completes `finalize`, including its browser gate, with identical HTML bytes.
- Regression tests: `test/lifecycle-layout.test.mjs` **15/15**, plus geometry, public artifact checker, workflow trunks, label clearance, layout rules and `test/lifecycle-junction.test.mjs` **291/291**; no skips. Negative overlap and downstream-row/self-loop cases remain covered. Independent code review found no remaining blocker.
- Golden checks and Gallery freshness pass. All ten fixed representative lifecycle inputs still pass the artifact checker and produce byte-identical HTML to `b43bf56c`. Private inputs and screenshots remain local.
- Perceptual review of the two dense-label repros: Classic at 1440/light and 1024/dark, with notes also inspected at the full-detail zoom.
- Only `archify.zip` required regeneration. Official Node **22.23.2**, bundled zlib **1.3.1-e00f703**: two builds byte-identical, SHA-256 `77ca5a5aaef54379e585b693e707ceb39f7d9842a952f30a133bda926ce31d61`. All three repros validate using the extracted package outside the repository.
- Final-head full CI: [run 37622913796](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/37622913796), head `b2eedd555cad7967d345dbc63cfe03ce50324106`, **passed**: Node 18/20/22/24 full tests, real browser regression, WebM/site-language integration, ZIP freshness, Linux/macOS/Windows package smoke, Windows path portability and website gates.

#### Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. The two added commits can be reverted.

**Blast Radius:** geometry. Dense lower-row layout changes only for the affected parallel groups; the shared checker exception requires an explicit common junction and source port. Ordinary lifecycle examples, README imagery and the website are unchanged by these two fixes.

items.title: fix(check): unify SVG path parsing and preserve subpath boundaries
items.body:
## Problem and value

Closes #641.

The public artifact checker can hang on incomplete SVG path parameters and can treat separate moveto subpaths as connected. It also closes later subpaths against the wrong origin and drops uppercase numeric exponents. These failures can block ordinary delivery or reject valid artifacts for geometry that is not drawn.

Use one terminating parser for the existing `M/L/H/V/Q/Z` subset and carry continuous drawing pieces through the checker. This keeps the fix within the agreed inspected-path scope without adding a general SVG engine. Latest `dev` is merged into the branch.

## Stability impact

- **Shared behavior:** artifact checking used by `check`, `validate`, `deliver`, and `compare`. Renderer layout, Viewer behavior, schemas, versions, and release identities are unchanged relative to the current target base.
- Inspected relationship/frame paths with malformed syntax or unsupported `A/C/S/T` commands fail with `artifact/svg-path-malformed` or `artifact/svg-path-unsupported`. The failed `svg_path_data` check and public CLI diagnostics include the path index, role, available ID, command, and decoded-data offset. Valid artifacts retain the existing nine checks.
- Moveto gaps and non-collinear `Q` gaps never create synthetic straight connections. Route budgets aggregate by relationship; label checks preserve identity deduplication; empty final subpaths and actual terminal pieces retain marker-end behavior. Legacy single-path metadata, provenance, crossover halos, authored direct routes, and quality thresholds remain supported.
- Decorative/icon/brand paths remain outside the inspected subset. Existing quadratic sampling and collinear-Q behavior are retained. Readable-v2's existing omission of non-collinear Q curve-body crossings remains outside this focused change; no claim of complete curve analysis is made.
- The delivery contract includes the complete English rules and a collapsible Chinese explanation. The full `deliver` integration test has a larger per-call watchdog; single-checker termination limits are unchanged.

## Tests run

Comparison base: `98c839a43eedb95f38700aa5243ea778c0482777` (`dev`). Candidate: `aef1a3f6c9c5ff002c7e562c1977f03195faee29`. Official Node 22.23.1 with zlib `1.3.1-e00f703`.

- Public CLI TDD: the two curved-route regressions fail on current `dev` and the previously reviewed implementation. They expose a phantom crossing/label obstruction and a missed real crossing on the post-curve straight segment. Both pass on the candidate; an additional control preserves empty terminal subpaths.
- Full `npm test`: **2,463 passed, 0 failed, 89 skipped**, 282.1 s. Includes parser termination/arity, relative commands, M/Z semantics, path diagnostics, `deliver` rollback, geometry, shared workflow trunks, canonical source freshness, release identity, and the new regressions. Optional browser/platform skips are not passes.
- **25/25 current-base compatibility cases** have identical complete public-check JSON receipts and exit codes: seven shipped HTML examples, all 12 Gallery artifacts, comparison HTML, a real architecture case, and four required/missing provenance cases.
- Syntax checks, `git diff --check`, byte-identical repeated canonical ZIP builds, and extracted-package smoke tests passed on macOS without installed package dependencies.

Focused reproduction:

```sh
cd archify
npm ci
node --test test/svg-path-analysis.test.mjs test/svg-path-checker.test.mjs \
  test/render-output-checks.test.mjs test/workflow-shared-trunks.test.mjs
npm test
```

Hosted [CI run 37185277736](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/37185277736) completed successfully on the candidate head: Node 18/20/22/24, Windows portability, WebM, ZIP freshness, manifest, scope and package smoke checks passed; website and Pages deployment were skipped by the workflow. CodeRabbit also confirmed the three review fixes. These checks do not establish browser/perceptual acceptance or maintainer approval.

## Generated artifacts

Rebuilt `archify.zip` from the final combined source twice; both archives are byte-identical. SHA-256: `0b67e6aa8db863eeb9470b8c0c5bea4f7ad52324e3bf3409e8c2450bc98d1e0e`. The extracted archive contains 119 entries, no installed dependencies or untracked evidence, and passes `scripts/package-smoke.mjs` outside the repository.

items.title: perf(compile): index the repeated scene scans in the workflow compiler and architecture label placement
items.body:
## Problem and value

Compile time on the documents a real repository produces is spent in repeated whole-scene scans rather than in any single expensive step. Two measured cases on `dev` @ `629155a` (Windows 11, Node 24, median of 3 runs of `node archify/bin/archify.mjs render <type> <doc> <out>`):

- a 384-node workflow document took **15.6 s**, a 768-node one **68.1 s**;
- an architecture document for a real repository (24 components, 26 connections, 65 source citations) took **7.47 s** end to end.

Intended outcome: the same artifacts, byte for byte, with the compile step no longer the noticeable cost.

The changes are local indexes and precomputations: a uniform grid for the obstacles, routes and labels one route already touches, a per-node endpoint index for the port search, memoized route normalization and text measurement, a bounded clearance test wherever only a threshold was compared, and one batched Git session for source evidence. No new configuration, no new file, and no output change.

Scope: `archify/renderers/**` (workflow compiler, shared geometry, architecture label placement, shared evidence helper, shared text measurement), plus the regenerated `archify.zip`.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: shared behavior — `renderers/shared/geometry.mjs` and `renderers/shared/repository-evidence.mjs` are used by all five diagram types.
- Changed behavior: none observable. Exit code, artifact SHA-256 and stderr diagnostics are identical for 19 documents (all five types, including two documents that must be rejected) before and after each step.
- Existing behavior preserved: schemas, defaults, diagnostics, rejection thresholds and Skill instructions are untouched.
- Failure behavior: identical diagnostics and exit codes; the batched Git session falls back to the per-citation calls and reuses the same messages.

## Tests run

Comparison base `629155a` (dev) → candidate head `perf/compile-speed`.

- 19-document corpus (exit code + artifact SHA-256 + stderr hash): identical for every document, before and after each step. Per document this is `node archify/bin/archify.mjs render <type> <doc> /tmp/out.html` on the base and on the candidate, then comparing `sha256sum /tmp/out.html`; the two examples that carry repository evidence also need `--repo-root`.
- Suites: `workflow-compiler-hard-contract`, `geometry`, `architecture-automatic-labels` — 168/168.
- Full local suite (Windows 11): 2547 tests, 2365 pass, 54 fail on the candidate; the same runner on the base `629155a` reports 2301 tests, 2119 pass, 63 fail. Those failures are Windows symlink, hard-link and permission cases that also fail on the base.
- Workflow compile: 384 nodes 15.6 s → **0.81 s**; 768 nodes 68.1 s → **1.34 s**.
- Architecture with source evidence (24 components, 65 citations): 7.47 s → **0.55 s**; that step went from about 130 `git` processes to one `cat-file --batch` session.
- Architecture with duplicated components: 96 components 1.07 s → **0.51 s**; 192 components 6.45 s → **1.19 s**; the growth exponent in the component count went from about 2.9 to about 1.2.

## Generated artifacts

- `archify.zip` regenerated with the canonical toolchain (`bash scripts/build-zip.sh`, Node 22) because renderer sources changed.
- `archify/assets/template.html` and the Viewer sources are untouched.
