items.title: perf(architecture): route, label, and fit first drafts without manual repairs
items.body:
## Problem and value

On current `dev`, an architecture first draft written with only automatic routes (no `via`/`fromSide`/`labelAt`/`labelDy`) routinely fails showcase validation on renderer geometry rather than on anything the author decided: automatic labels land on nodes, corridors become ambiguous, compiler-fit canvases clip outer routes, and tall diagrams overflow the viewport with no readable-scroll option. Each failure costs the authoring agent a candidate edit plus a full validate/deliver/check/visual-check round.

Measured on one real-repository task (evermemos-mcp, 6.3k lines Python, same prompt, same model, isolated skill packages, serial runs):

| Package | Wall | Candidate edits after first full write | CLI rounds | Manual route controls in final JSON |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| `dev` fork point `31bfbc8e` | 713 s | 7 (5 renderer geometry, 2 late visual-check overflow) | validate×9, deliver/check/visual-check ×3 each | 5 |
| `labs/first-draft-cost-20260918` renderer layer | 343 s | 1 (schema limits, not geometry) | finalize×2 | 0 |

Direct replay on `dev` vs this branch with the two first drafts the perf package accepted:

| First draft | `dev` validate | this branch validate |
|---|---|---|
| B (9 nodes, 12 edges, automatic routes) | fail: `clean-flow/edge-through-node`, 2× `composition/label-route-clearance`, 2× `layout/constraint` | pass |
| C (9 nodes, 12 edges, automatic routes) | fail: 13 diagnostics (endpoint-side-direction, proper-crossing, ambiguous-corridor, 6× label-route-clearance, 3× layout/constraint) | pass |

The branch's own 36-run study (`benchmarks/authoring-cost/results.md` on the labs branch) points the same direction: post-JSON time per run fell from a 57–69 s median to 15–27 s once these renderer changes were in place.

This PR carries **only the renderer, checker, viewer, and visual-check portion** of `labs/first-draft-cost-20260918`. The `finalize`/`browser-check` CLI and the SKILL.md restructuring are deferred to a separate PR because they conflict with the Windows path contracts (#476) in `archify.mjs`/`cli.mjs`; the renderer layer merges cleanly.

Source commits: `a2158997..4fb530ea` cherry-picked; renderer hunks of `8d22a944`, `95170f3f`, `31fa93c5`, `d21948a7` re-applied by path.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: **shared behavior** (architecture geometry, shared route-quality/readability checks, Viewer reader layout, visual-check browser probe).
- Changed behavior:
  - Architecture automatic routing plans connections against already-resolved routes and rejects side pairs whose segments would overlap or touch them; automatic label placement considers the full route set (`routing.mjs`, `labels.mjs`).
  - Canvas fitting includes outer route corridors; compiler-measured architectures fit desktop height; tall diagrams may declare readable vertical scroll (`fit-or-reader-declared-readable-vertical-scroll` containment policy in visual-check).
  - New showcase diagnostics: `composition/excessive-route-detour` and related clean-route detour checks (`route-quality.mjs`), boundary repair evidence on failed geometry.
  - Desktop readability is measured against the declared wide Reader contract (`archify-reader-contract: declared-wide-v1` meta), edge/boundary labels are reported as their own owners, and `composition/desktop-readability` fixes state the maximum viewBox width numerically.
  - Viewer exposes `Archify.layoutStability.whenStable`; visual-check waits once for reader layout + viewer chrome + fonts instead of four fixed waits. Slow Chrome startup (`Target.getTargets` > `CHROME_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` = 90 s) is reported as `viewer/chrome-startup-timeout` with "do not edit the artifact" guidance.
  - Automatic crossover mask underlays are wrapped in a presentation-only group so the checker scans them once and reader states mirror the semantic edge; exports and graph traversal still see exactly one edge per relationship.
- Preserved: schema v1 unchanged; explicit geometry remains authoritative; `standard` profile unchanged; existing showcase codes unchanged; non-zero exits and `diagnostics[]` receipts preserved. Checked-in examples re-render with the same topology (see Generated artifacts).
- Compatibility notes: artifacts rendered before this change have no reader contract and are judged with the legacy 930 px readability budget by the new checker; the old arm-A artifact above fails `composition/desktop-readability` (5.5 px projected text) under the new checker while passing its own. That is the intended tightening — the old renderer let authors shrink text below the 6 px floor to satisfy viewport fit.
- Test adaptations to `dev`: fixtures gain the now-required `meta.output`; the joint-wait contract tests exercise `runVisualCheck` (the deferred `runBrowserCheck` does not exist here); `chrome-pipe-transport.test.mjs` derives its first-command timeout from `CHROME_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS`.

## Tests run

Remote CI on final head `d42243ecee0146c92596e5a5c27c9fa87c0154b3`: [run 35751853476](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/35751853476) completed successfully. All 14 active jobs passed: scope; published-update-manifest; website; zip-freshness; package smoke (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows); test (Node 18, 20, 22, 24); Windows test portability (Node 22, 24); webm-artifact (real WebM decode and shared browser regression gate). deploy-pages was intentionally skipped for this PR.

The Linux return-state failure in prior run 35750261802 was isolated to the generated legend (maximum 0.27 px; reader width 1068 px and authored semantic/frame state unchanged). Commit `d42243ec` bounds only that runtime legend's return comparison to 0.5 px while retaining exact authored-state checks and the exact within-state convergence gate. The focused local Chrome suite also passed 8/8.

Base `origin/dev` @ `5c878178`; candidate head is this branch. Node 22.23.2, Chrome 152, macOS arm64.

- `cd archify && npm test` — 2112 pass, 0 fail, 74 optional skips (includes viewer/brand-marks/validators/release-identity freshness and golden renders).
- `ARCHIFY_CHROME=… npm run test:browser` — 240/240.
- `ARCHIFY_CHROME=… npm run test:webm` — WebM smoke + 7 site-language tests pass.
- `ARCHIFY_MCO_REPO_ROOT=<pinned mco clone> node --test test/real-repository-proof.test.mjs` — passes after re-rendering the MCO case/showcase.
- `scripts/build-zip.sh` twice under Node 22 — byte-identical.
- Real-repository replay described above (evermemos-mcp @ `1d565111`, read-only worktree): both perf-package first drafts validate and deliver on this branch; `visual-check` passes at all four viewports, min projected text 6 px+.

Gaps: single task / single model for the wall-clock figures (direction only, not a percentage claim); no Windows or Linux run locally — CI covers those.

## Visual evidence

- Evidence: 1440×900 light captures of the replayed first drafts on this branch match the perf-package renders pixel-for-pixel in topology, routes and labels (attached in review if requested; produced by `visual-check`). Intended differences from `dev`: automatic labels no longer overlap endpoints; no manual route controls needed.
- Comparison conditions: same JSON, 1440×900 / 2048×1320, light+dark, Classic preset, architecture mode, 100% zoom, initial page state.
- Automated or browser checks: `visual-check` pass (containment, readability, viewer chrome) for both drafts; browser suites above.
- Perceptual visual review: passed (author reviewed the 1440×900 light captures of both replayed drafts and the re-rendered `web-app` example).

## Follow-up: replaying the repair-study first drafts (commits `7b5b71c7`, `3f72d760`)

Twelve unmodified first drafts from the Sol/Terra/Luna repair study (9 architecture, 3 workflow; the study ran on `355b6096`) were replayed against this branch with `validate --quality showcase`. Four architecture drafts that declared **no route controls at all** still failed on routes the router itself had chosen:

| Draft | Failure on `dev`/branch before | Root cause | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| audit-luna | `container-border-run` 31px + `short-interior-segment` 10px (12-point staircase) | grid shortest path hugs obstacle edges; router unaware of frame borders and rhythm floors | pass, 4-point route |
| audit-terra | `micro-segment` 3px | cheap dogleg accepted without the 8px floor | pass |
| queue-sol | `container-border-run` 42px | dogleg mid-x landed exactly on the boundary right border | pass |
| queue-luna | `layout/constraint` "place its components farther apart" on a worker→worker self-loop | inapplicable message for a self-loop with `fromSide/toSide: bottom` | `layout/self-loop-ports` names the loop and the fix; passes once the sides are removed |
| release-luna (workflow) | one overlap pair per round (7 pairs in the draft) | compiler failed on the first pair | all 7 pairs in one round |

Changes: the router applies the composition floors (frame border runs, 8px/16px segment floors) to every candidate before accepting it; the grid search treats frame borders as uncrossable lengthwise, coalesces to the 16px interior floor, penalises bends (48px) and never reverses along a stub; labels of already-routed relationships are reserved while later automatic routes are planned (with a detour guard so a reservation never forces a long perimeter route). Shipped examples, gallery and goldens are byte-identical: the change only alters routes the gate would have rejected or arbitrary tie-breaks among equal-length detours.

Fresh authoring runs on this head (same tasks/fixtures as the study, new SWE-model contexts, no route controls allowed unless asked): audit export — validate/deliver/check/visual-check all pass first time, 0 repairs, ~2.5 min; queue gateway — 1 repair (author used a filesystem path as `meta.repository.url`), then pass, ~6 min. In the study the same two tasks cost 0–3 repairs per model with 3/6 not delivering.

Tests on this head: `npm test` 2124 pass / 0 fail (Node 22), browser gate 241/241, WebM gate pass, ZIP rebuilt twice byte-identical. New fixtures: `test/fixtures/architecture-first-draft/*`, `test/fixtures/workflow-first-draft/release-luna.workflow.json`, `test/fixtures/lifecycle-planner/approval.lifecycle.json`.

## Generated artifacts

Regenerated from combined source: `archify/assets/template.html` (`npm run generate:viewer`), `archify/examples/*.html` and `examples/*.html` (`render:examples`), `examples/web-app.html` (copy of `web-app-rendered.html`), `docs/gallery/**` + `docs/gallery.html` + `docs/guide.html` + `docs/start.html`, `docs/assets/archify-live-proof.{gif,json}` (`build-readme-showcase`), `examples/checkout-platform-delta.{html,receipt.json}` (`compare`), `docs/cases/mco-runtime.architecture.html` and `experiments/mco-showcase/mco-runtime.html` (`deliver`/`render` against the pinned MCO revision), `archify.zip` (Node 22, reproducible).

Generated with [Devin](https://devin.ai)
## Update: two follow-up commits from the rework-reduction pass

While replaying the maintainer's two "year-long holiday timeline" retrospectives (both lost most of their time to a vertical overflow that only surfaced at the last gate), this branch gained:

**`4ec10226` fix(viewer): settle the adaptive reader when card height follows its width.** A portrait architecture with conclusion cards oscillated forever between two reader widths (883px ↔ 858px at 2048×1320): `measure()` derived width from the current card height, `settleOverflow()` narrowed, cards rewrapped shorter, `measure()` widened again. `dev` reports "Adaptive reader layout did not reach stable dimensions"; the joint wait times out at 15 s and visual-check returns a Chrome runtime failure instead of a layout verdict. Fix: cap `measure()` at the widest width the settle has accepted for this viewport (reset on resize). Red/green: `test/reader-layout-settle-browser.test.mjs` fails on the previous template and passes with the cap. Also: `viewer/viewport-overflow` receipts now carry `pageComposition` (body padding / header / guided views / diagram chrome / SVG / cards, summing to `scrollHeight`) and state the pixel budget and target instead of "contain the rendered layout within 1440x900".

**`ffd68ef2` feat(check): predict fixed-width viewport overflow before the browser gate.** A canvas with viewBox ratio < 1.55 and no `data-reader-fit="intrinsic-height"` renders at the full 1346px reader width at 1440×900, so its page height is a pure function of the viewBox: `1346 × h/w + 126px` (+61px with guided views). The shared checker now reports `composition/viewport-height` with the maximum viewBox height at the current width / minimum width at the current height. Prediction matches Chrome to the pixel on the three gallery artifacts that fail visual-check today (`event-stream.dataflow` 972px, `incident-response.workflow` 1683px, `deployment-release.lifecycle` 934px SVG). Per CONTRIBUTING it is a **warning** in every profile for now: existing artifacts and the gallery build keep passing, showcase authors see the non-zero warning count with the executable fix in `composition.issues[].detail`.

Finding for maintainers (not changed here): five gallery artifacts (`async-job-roundtrip.sequence`, `deployment-release.lifecycle`, `event-stream.dataflow`, `incident-response.workflow`, `release-delivery.workflow`) are portrait and fail `visual-check` at 1440×900 today, while the gallery labels them "SHOWCASE · PASS". Sequence, dataflow and lifecycle renderers never declare `intrinsic-height`, so a portrait diagram in those modes currently has no way to pass the browser gate; that is a contract decision (an explicit readable-scroll intent) rather than a checker fix.

Evidence on the final head `ffd68ef2` (Node 22): `npm test` 2115 pass / 0 fail / 75 optional skips; `npm run test:browser` 241/241; `npm run test:webm` 7/7; ZIP byte-identical across two builds.
## Update: lifecycle first drafts (`73369100`, `1dbe…`)

Replaying a lifecycle authoring task exposed the next rework generator: a lifecycle first draft that leaves routing to the renderer **could not pass showcase at all**. On `dev`, the fixture `test/fixtures/lifecycle-planner/review-hub.lifecycle.json` (7 states, 7 transitions, no route controls) returns 2× `clean-flow/edge-through-node`, 4× `composition/micro-segment` and several `label-route-clearance` errors, and the default 980×660 canvas (ratio 1.48, no Reader fit) overflows 1440×900 by construction. Every shipped lifecycle example hand-routes all of its transitions, so authoring agents copy that and then fight `clean-flow/endpoint-side-direction` — one replayed agent spent 14 minutes after its first draft doing exactly this.

Changes:
- Transitions without `via`/`route`/`channelX`/`channelY` are routed by the obstacle-aware planner already shared with architecture (`createRouter`), render with the same crossover mask wrapper (planner crossings resolve instead of failing), and showcase labels use `placeAutomaticLabels`. Authored via/route-preset/channel geometry and authored viewBoxes keep the lifecycle presets byte-for-byte; golden examples unchanged.
- A renderer-sized lifecycle canvas declares `data-reader-fit="intrinsic-height"` like architecture; the desktop Reader then narrows it (1153px at 1440×900) instead of overflowing.
- Shared grid search coalesces grid lines closer than 8px so it stops emitting micro jogs between adjacent obstacle edges.
- SKILL.md: the first-draft rule now also names `route`, `fromSide`, `toSide`; the Lifecycle note states the shared middle band.

End-to-end replay (same prompt, fresh subagent, same model, this package): **validate ×2, deliver ×1, check ×1, visual-check ×1 — one real repair round (a genuine authoring error: two side states on the same band position), 545 s, all gates pass**, vs. the previous run that never delivered after 22 minutes and 7+ validation attempts. Visual review of the 1440×900 capture: readable, all states/transitions present; two planner detours are longer than a hand route would be (noted, not a gate failure).

Evidence on the final head (Node 22): `npm test` 2116 pass / 0 fail / 75 optional skips; `npm run test:browser` 241/241; ZIP rebuilt and reproducible.

items.title: fix(viewer): preserve Finder IME composition
items.body:
## Problem and value

Fixes #902. While an IME is composing Chinese, Japanese, or other input, its Enter confirmation was treated as a Finder selection command. The Finder closed and selected the first visible node before the input method could commit its candidate. The Viewer now leaves composing key events to the input method, preserving the existing post-composition keyboard workflow.

## Stability impact

- Impact class and changed behavior/shared callers: local Viewer input handling in `viewer/node-finder.js`; bundled Viewer artifacts are regenerated.
- Existing behavior preserved / intended compatibility changes / failure behavior: ordinary ArrowDown and Enter behavior remains unchanged after composition ends. The new guard only returns for `event.isComposing`.

## Tests run

Base: `d5806a6f8d05900fab175b832020f2da32f4152f`; head: `5e0d26a6eff8345366397b5e7a37b692dfb4b1d6`.

- `npm run test:generated` passed.
- `ARCHIFY_CHROME="C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" npm run test:browser -- test/finder-browser.test.mjs` passed (real Chrome; all five diagram modes).
- The regression dispatches a composing Enter and verifies that Finder remains open, input focus is preserved, and default is not prevented; the following ordinary Enter still selects the result.

## Generated artifacts

Regenerated the Viewer template, root and packaged rendered examples, Gallery page/artifacts/manifest, Architecture Delta example/receipt, and deterministic Node 22 `archify.zip` from the final source.
